starter.README.md:
# Programming Jokes

Display one programming joke as a setup followed by its punchline. The supplied set has ten actual programming jokes from the original API project's public data. Saved responses cycle through those records. Live API requests use the original programming/random endpoint; a successful response may be an object or a one-item array. Keep its two pieces of text together.

Complete loadJokeResponse, normalizeJoke and renderJoke in script.js. In the asynchronous loader, await fixtureResponse for saved data or await requestJson for the live endpoint, then return the validated record from its data field. Normalize an array by selecting its first record, reject empty data, and require nonempty setup and punchline strings of at most 500 characters. The supplied request.js checks HTTP status, JSON content type, a 512 KiB response limit and a four-second deadline. Parse and validate before changing the page. Use textContent and replace the previous two paragraphs instead of accumulating old output. A supplied color rule keeps the original colored-text idea while retaining readable contrast.

Select Saved responses and load several jokes without a network. Then select Live API and inspect the request in the browser tools. One active request is allowed; Cancel aborts it. A failed or malformed refresh keeps the previous joke and shows a status. Random endpoints deliberately request a fresh value, while the shared helper retains a bounded cache for deterministic lookups. Check CASES.md before comparing the completed reference. Open index.html without a server.

The starter supplies the request and interface wiring;complete loadJokeResponse, normalizeJoke, renderJoke before comparing the reference.
starter.CASES.md:
# Programming Jokes cases

1. Cycle ten saved records offline; setup and punchline remain paired.
2. Both object and one-item-array live shapes render one joke.
3. Empty, malformed, missing fields, invalid JSON, oversized and non-JSON responses preserve the previous result.
4. HTTP503, network failure, timeout and Cancel show a status.
5. Repeated loading clicks create one active request; a late canceled response cannot replace newer work.
6. Markup-shaped joke text displays literally; mobile and enlarged text reflow.

starter.index.html: Random Fox Generator
starter.README.md:
# Random Fox Generator

Add a fox photograph whenever the load button succeeds. Each valid response appends a fox photograph to the gallery. The gallery retains the newest twelve entries. Saved responses cycle through three real, public-domain fox photographs; their credits and source pages are included. Live API uses the original randomfox.ca/floof/ endpoint when available.

Complete loadFoxResponse, validateFox and appendFox in script.js. The asynchronous loader selects fixtureResponse or requestJson and returns the validated object before image decoding begins. Require an object with a valid image field. Saved image values must match the supplied fixtures; live values must use HTTPS, the exact randomfox.ca origin and an images/number.jpg, .jpeg or .png path. Reject query strings, fragments and unrelated origins. The supplied request helper checks status, JSON parsing, byte size and a four-second deadline. The supplied image helper waits for successful decoding before the new figure is attached, so broken images cannot displace valid ones.

Create meaningful alt text from trusted local copy, keep image proportions with CSS, and append a text credit link. Remove the oldest figure only after a thirteenth valid result is ready. Verify the gallery offline, then use Cancel and the failure cases in CASES.md. Failed requests or image loads keep earlier photographs. Photographs use their natural proportions at both display widths. Open index.html without a server.

The starter supplies the request and interface wiring;complete loadFoxResponse, validateFox, appendFox before comparing the reference.
starter.CASES.md:
# Random Fox Generator cases

1. Three supplied real photographs load with alt text and credits offline.
2. Thirteen valid loads retain the newest twelve figures.
3. Invalid protocol, origin, path, malformed data and unexpected image URLs append nothing.
4. An allowed URL with a failed image response keeps existing photographs.
5. HTTP403, timeout, Cancel and malformed JSON leave earlier results visible.
6. Image proportions, credits, keyboard control and enlarged text remain usable at both widths.

starter.index.html: Pokedex
starter.README.md:
# Pokedex

Search the original 893-entry Pokémon index by name or numeric ID. Every entry includes its real name, one or two types, six base statistics and the corresponding supplied sprite. The local dataset is derived from pinned public PokéAPI CSV files and sprite sources, so every indexed lookup works offline. The datalist contains all 893 names. Live API optionally refreshes one selected record; loading the page never launches 893 requests.

Complete loadPokemonResponse, normalizePokemon and renderPokemon in script.js. The asynchronous loader selects the saved record or one live request, waits for validation, and returns its data plus cache status. Require an ID from 1 through 893, a normalized name, one or two type records, six numeric base statistics and a valid sprite. The complete reference accepts the supplied PNG data URLs locally and the exact reviewed PokéAPI sprite path for a live response. Render one result with DOM text, a labeled sprite and a definition list of statistics; replace previous details so repeated searches do not accumulate stale fields.

The supplied request.js checks HTTP status, JSON type, a 512 KiB response cap, one active request and a four-second timeout. Successful live records enter a bounded sixty-second cache. Repeating the same lookup uses it; a failed refresh retains the previous record. Try bulbasaur, pikachu, 25 and 893, then an unknown name. Inspect CASES.md, including markup-shaped input, invalid records, sprite failure and cached reads. Open index.html without a server.

The starter supplies the request and interface wiring;complete loadPokemonResponse, normalizePokemon, renderPokemon before comparing the reference.
starter.CASES.md:
# Pokedex cases

1. Every ID1–893 has its correct name,two-or-fewer types,six stats and actual PNG sprite.
2. Name and numeric-ID lookup agree; repeat searches replace the sole result.
3. A cached live lookup makes no second request during sixty seconds.
4. Invalid name/ID, malformed stats, foreign sprite origin or empty response keep the last record.
5. HTTP404/503, timeout, Cancel and image failure show readable status.
6. Datalist has893 unique names; images and all six statistics remain visible offline and at200% text.

reference.README.md:
# Pokedex

Search the original 893-entry Pokémon index by name or numeric ID. Every entry includes its real name, one or two types, six base statistics and the corresponding supplied sprite. The local dataset is derived from pinned public PokéAPI CSV files and sprite sources, so every indexed lookup works offline. The datalist contains all 893 names. Live API optionally refreshes one selected record; loading the page never launches 893 requests.

Complete loadPokemonResponse, normalizePokemon and renderPokemon in script.js. The asynchronous loader selects the saved record or one live request, waits for validation, and returns its data plus cache status. Require an ID from 1 through 893, a normalized name, one or two type records, six numeric base statistics and a valid sprite. The complete reference accepts the supplied PNG data URLs locally and the exact reviewed PokéAPI sprite path for a live response. Render one result with DOM text, a labeled sprite and a definition list of statistics; replace previous details so repeated searches do not accumulate stale fields.

The supplied request.js checks HTTP status, JSON type, a 512 KiB response cap, one active request and a four-second timeout. Successful live records enter a bounded sixty-second cache. Repeating the same lookup uses it; a failed refresh retains the previous record. Try bulbasaur, pikachu, 25 and 893, then an unknown name. Inspect CASES.md, including markup-shaped input, invalid records, sprite failure and cached reads. Open index.html without a server.

The reference completes loadPokemonResponse, normalizePokemon, renderPokemon for comparison after the starter attempt.
reference.CASES.md:
# Pokedex cases

1. Every ID1–893 has its correct name,two-or-fewer types,six stats and actual PNG sprite.
2. Name and numeric-ID lookup agree; repeat searches replace the sole result.
3. A cached live lookup makes no second request during sixty seconds.
4. Invalid name/ID, malformed stats, foreign sprite origin or empty response keep the last record.
5. HTTP404/503, timeout, Cancel and image failure show readable status.
6. Datalist has893 unique names; images and all six statistics remain visible offline and at200% text.

starter.README.md:
# Funny Meter

Rate exactly ten programming jokes, one at a time. This optional project extends the single-joke reader: the completed normalizeJoke helper is supplied, and the new work is validating the batch and recording decisions. Saved responses contain ten actual programming jokes. The Live API option uses the original programming/ten endpoint when available.

Complete loadTenJokesResponse, normalizeTenJokes and recordRating in script.js. The asynchronous loader awaits the saved response or the live programming/ten endpoint before creating the session. Require an array of exactly ten valid jokes, assign a stable session ID to each position, and reuse normalizeJoke for each setup and punchline. Store each accepted rating with the current joke's ID. Accept only yes or no; invalid input leaves the current position unchanged. The next joke is determined by the number of recorded ratings, not by an independently incremented prompt counter.

The supplied renderer shows progress, the current joke and two native answer buttons. After ten answers it displays liked/disliked counts and whether the set was liked, disliked or tied. Buttons stop accepting ratings at completion. Restart clears ratings for the current set; a failed live refresh preserves it, and another load cannot erase a partly rated session. Use CASES.md to complete all-yes, all-no and tied sessions, plus invalid/duplicate/after-completion cases. Open index.html without a server.

The starter supplies the request and interface wiring;complete loadTenJokesResponse, normalizeTenJokes, recordRating before comparing the reference.
starter.CASES.md:
# Funny Meter cases

1. Ten yes ratings give10liked/0disliked;ten no ratings give0/10;five each give an even split.
2. Invalid/canceled answers do not advance;every accepted rating retains its joke ID.
3. Further ratings after ten are ignored.
4. Restart clears ratings but retains the current ten jokes.
5. A partial session rejects another load;failed refresh retains the existing set.
6. Short/long arrays,invalid joke fields,HTTP503,timeout and Cancel are handled without an unhandled error.
